public_rationale: The searches do not establish that the White House had done nothing. A readable secondary account describes a September 24 report that the White House sought US testing before models were shared with British testers. That is potentially relevant action, but its timing and connection to these incidents are insufficiently established. Neither a decisive contradiction nor reliable evidence of no action was obtained.
limitations: Private government activity cannot be excluded through public searches.
The available counterevidence is secondary and rests on reporting whose original pages could not be read.
Actions taken after the post cannot settle what was true when Marcus wrote it.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The White House has taken no action over OpenAI's hacking incidents.

statement.excerpt: And so far the White House has done nothing.
statement.document_title: “I think the answer is we have to shut the labs down” - Jensen Huang

our_interpretation: Read the claim as no publicly documented substantive White House response to the OpenAI hacking incidents by the post's publication.
A substantive response could include an inquiry, mitigation requirement, testing restriction, or enforcement measure. It need not be the shutdown Marcus recommends.
Congressional or state action does not automatically count as White House action.
For this ongoing state, use September 24 as the latest publicly observable reporting day before publication. Assess cumulative action as of that day.
An action reported on September 24 requires evidence that it preceded the post; the supplied post metadata does not give a publication time.
criteria.support_condition: Authoritative contemporaneous accounts or sufficiently complete records establish that no substantive White House response had occurred by publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A dated record establishes a substantive White House action addressing these incidents that was already taken by publication.
